newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand asks Cambodia to protect foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Thailand asks Cambodia to protect foreigners.

text.p: Thailand asked Cambodia on Tuesday to take urgent measures to ensure the safety of foreign nationals caught in fighting between warring factions in Phnom Penh.

"The Royal Thai Government is gravely concerned with the armed conflict...which has resulted in losses of lives of Cambodians as well as foreigners and damage to their property," said a foreign ministry statement.
"The latest incident has seriously undermined the well-being of the Cambodian people as well as peace and stability of the region as a whole," it added.
Thailand wanted all parties in Cambodia to resolve differences by peaceful means and to abide by provisions of the 1991 Paris peace accords that officially ended the country's civil war.
Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh and took control of the government after heavy fighting in Phnom Penh between their two forces.
Phnom Penh has been gripped by looting and gunfire after the weekend fighting. Thailand sent planes on Tuesday to evacuate its citizens and other nationals from the Cambodian capital.

The statement said that Thailand, in view of the latest developments, would closely monitor the situation in Cambodia and consult with ASEAN countries on the question of the timing of Cambodia's entry into the group as a new member.
The seven-member Association of South East Asian Nations groups Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, the Philippines, Vietnam and Brunei.
Cambodia was due to be admitted as a new member later this month.
